text: sterculia have been used in an attempt to control appetite by the local effect they might exert when they swell in the gastrointestinal tract, but there is little ev- idence of efficacy. Nondigestible fat substitutes such as su- crose polyesters have been promoted by the food industry, as part of a strategy to reduce fat and calories in the diet to aid body-weight control. The control of appetite and the mechanisms of obesity are under investigation. A gene, called the ob-gene, and its protein product, leptin, have been identified and appear to be involved in regulation of food intake. References. 1. Epstein LH, et al.
